name: Seared halibut with persimmon and fennel salad
intro: California halibut is in season now. Sear it the way October taught — dry fish, hot pan, hands off — and serve it beside a cold salad of Fuyu persimmon and fennel, shaved thin with lemon and Parmesan.
needs: 1 lb halibut (or lingcod, or rockfish), about 1 inch thick, in two pieces
1 fennel bulb, shaved thin (keep the fronds)
1 oz Parmesan, shaved with a peeler
Rice: about 1 cup cooked per serving

steps.text: Salt the fish and leave it on a plate. Pat it completely dry right before it goes in the pan.
Toss the fennel and persimmon with the juice of half the lemon, 2 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper. Scatter the Parmesan and fronds over the top.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a nonstick or well-seasoned skillet over medium-high until it shimmers. Lay the fish in, away from you, and leave it until the underside is golden and it releases on its own.
Flip and cook until the thickest part flakes when you press it (the USDA's safe temperature is 145°F). Thinner fillets take less.
Fish over rice, the salad beside it, the rest of the lemon squeezed over everything.

how_it_works: Lean, sweet fish wants something crisp and sweet-sharp beside it, not a heavy sauce. Halibut is firmer than October's rockfish, so it needs a few more minutes a side, but it's the same sear: the crust forms when you stop moving it. Fuyu persimmon is the rare fruit that's crisp enough to shave like a vegetable.
swaps: Lingcod or rockfish if the halibut is out; thinner fillets cook faster.
A forkful of pickled fennel in place of the raw fennel.
Satsuma segments in the salad instead of persimmon.
leftovers: Cook both pieces and keep one for lunch: cold, flaked over rice with the rest of the salad. Don't reheat it.
